UI-R2-M1.reasoning: nodeCertificateObservation.ts:56-62 forwards signal into apiClient, which spreads options into fetch (client.ts:202-205, unchanged). A hung or 60s-504 certificate leg is now aborted by the same 10s deadline; the abort rejection reaches the outer catch with signal.reason = Error('REQUEST_TIMEOUT') -> isTimeout -> nodesState error + '클러스터 노드 응답 시간 초과 (10s Timeout)' when the session/scope/applied fences pass. A non-abort certificate failure still yields certObs = null and a node success (unchanged R2 behaviour). Applied/session/scope fences and stale-retention (nodes not cleared on error) are unchanged, so recovery (next good tick applies) and late-response ignoring are preserved.

UI-R2-L1.source: App.tsx:376-382 (nodes), 431-437 (runs), 489-495 (approvals), 546-552 (workspaces): isTimeout = controller.signal.aborted && (reason?.message === 'REQUEST_TIMEOUT' || reason === 'REQUEST_TIMEOUT'); if aborted && !isTimeout -> return. The four R2 classifiers 'err?.name === AbortError || err?.message === REQUEST_TIMEOUT' are removed (0 remaining in App.tsx; reviewer regex).
UI-R2-L1.reasoning: The only REQUEST_TIMEOUT abort is the owner timer (4 sites); every other aborter (manual !isBg supersede 320-322/400-402/458-460/516-518, chooseProject 220-223, resetAuthenticatedState 141-144, unmount 578-585) calls abort() with no reason (DOMException AbortError), so they return without touching state and without the 10s banner. Each of those aborters sets its own state (superseder sets loading; chooseProject/logout reset to idle and bump scope/session/applied). A non-aborted rejection whose message is 'REQUEST_TIMEOUT' is not classified as timeout (isTimeout requires signal.aborted). Timer-owned hangs still become visible errors (P7, R1). finally clearTimeout and request > xAppliedRef fences unchanged. Older overlapping controllers (not in xAbortRef) keep their own deadline and are fenced; accepted bounded-overlap design not reopened.

UI-R2-L2.source: Header.tsx:52-54 4s timer; 58 fetch; 61 seq/mount fence after headers; 66-74 body read under the deadline, inner catch (69) rethrows when currentController.signal.aborted, otherwise data = null; 75 rtt after body; 76 seq/mount fence re-checked after body; 85-87 outer catch -> offline if current; 88-90 finally holds the only clearTimeout (count 1).
UI-R2-L2.reasoning: Healthy headers followed by a stalled body are aborted at 4s; the body rejection is rethrown to the outer catch -> 'Offline' (truthful transport/body failure). An older body completing after a newer check returns at the seq fence, so it cannot overwrite a newer failure. A malformed non-abort JSON body -> data null -> degraded ('비정상 응답'). Fetch-phase hang -> abort -> Offline. HTML 200 / JSON 404/503 / status!=ok remain degraded; network rejection remains Offline. 4s < 5s interval, so at most one check is normally in flight.
UI-R2-L2.tests: H3 (body hangs after headers: healthy RTT -> Offline, no ms label at +60s; with the R2 placement the label would stay healthy), H3b (malformed JSON -> 비정상 응답, not Offline; recovers to RTT), H4 (fetch hang -> Offline at 4.1s), H5 (503 -> RTT -> network Offline), H1 five classes, H2 (older slow success cannot overwrite newer Offline).
UI-R2-L2.limit: Body-phase stale-overwrite is covered by the post-body seq fence statically; H2 exercises the headers-phase variant. happy-dom fetch/Response, not a real browser body stream.

info: UI-R3-I1 (test precision, non-blocking): in R2b the mocked pending /nodes promise already rejects with signal.reason inside its abort listener when the manual refresh aborts it, so the later bgReq.reject(new Error('REQUEST_TIMEOUT')) is a no-op on a settled promise. R2b therefore proves supersede-with-AbortError is not a timeout (it would fail the R2 err.name classifier), but it does not exercise 'a late err.message REQUEST_TIMEOUT alone'. That property is established by the exact b48 source (no err.message/err.name classifier in any of the 4 catches). By static reasoning a re-added '|| err?.message === REQUEST_TIMEOUT' fallback would survive the current suite. Optional hardening: a pending mock that does not auto-reject on abort, so the late reject reaches the catch.

UI-R3-I2: T1 checks real-transport signal presence and aborted state on /node-certificates, /runs, /approvals, /workspaces but not abort reason or the resulting UI; the R2 reviewer T1 recorded REQUEST_TIMEOUT reasons on the primary legs. Combined with R1/R1b and source reading this is sufficient for M1 closure.
